decisions.rationale: Metagross + Whimsicott lead uses Prankster Tailwind to outspeed Floette/Garchomp/Talonflame. Whimsicott resists their key moves; Metagross threatens SE Ice Punch/Meteor Mash. Quaquaval + Archaludon back provide Water/Fighting and Steel/Dragon coverage for Rotom-Wash, Talonflame, Dragapult, and Annihilape.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Floette-Eternal (Mega, Light of Ruin, Flower Veil), Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin, EQ/Rock Slide), Rotom-Wash (Sitrus, Levitate, Hydro Pump/Volt Switch/Will-O-Wisp), Talonflame (Sharp Beak, Gale Wings, Brave Bird/Tailwind/Will-O-Wisp), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator, Dragon Darts/Phantom Force/Will-O-Wisp), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant, Rage Fist/Close Combat/U-turn). Intended Mega: Metagross. Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore critical for speed control and disrupting setup/status. Quaquaval Moxie snowball key if given free turns. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection if needed.

decisions.rationale: Mega Floette is the only Mega Stone holder. Talonflame's priority Tailwind (Gale Wings, 195 Spe beats Whimsicott 184 max) secures speed control turn 1. Floette Mega Evolves and fires Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin. Garchomp's Earthquake destroys Metagross/Archaludon/Stunfisk. Rotom-Wash provides Ground immunity, Will-o-Wisp for physical Steel-types, and Volt Switch to reposition. This mode handles both Prankster leads and keeps offensive momentum.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has two Prankster users (Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl) — expect one lead. Metagross is likely their Mega. Stunfisk-Galar has Mimicry (type changes to terrain). Archaludon has Stalwart (ignores redirection). Quaquaval has Moxie snowball potential. Respect Encore from Whimsicott when using Protect/Synthesis with Floette.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind sets up speed control for the team. Metagross Mega Evolves and attacks Floette-Eternal with super-effective Meteor Mash (59.7-301.7%, possible OHKO). Even if Talonflame outspeeds Whimsicott and uses Brave Bird, Whimsicott survives with Focus Sash and still sets up Tailwind. This line establishes speed control and applies pressure on Floette-Eternal, setting up Quaquaval Moxie snowball for later turns.
decisions.notebook: Opponent lead: Floette-Eternal (Mega, Light of Ruin, Flower Veil) + Talonflame (Sharp Beak, Gale Wings, Brave Bird). Talonflame Gale Wings Brave Bird has +1 priority, can OHKO Whimsicott but Focus Sash guarantees survival. Floette-Eternal attacks 0.5x on Metagross. Metagross-Mega Meteor Mash super-effective on Floette-Eternal (59.7-301.5%, possible OHKO). Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind critical for speed control. Quaquaval Moxie snowball key if given free turns. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection if needed. Opponent back: Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin, EQ/Rock Slide), Rotom-Wash (Sitrus, Levitate, Hydro Pump/Volt Switch/Will-O-Wisp), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator, Dragon Darts/Phantom Force/Will-O-Wisp), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant, Rage Fist/Close Combat/U-turn).

decisions.rationale: Floette is in immediate OHKO range from Mega Metagross Meteor Mash. Switching to Rotom-Wash absorbs the hit cleanly (4x Steel resist, Ground immune). Talonflame Tailwind at +1 priority outruns Whimsicott and ensures speed parity even if foe also Tailwinds. This preserves both Pokémon, gains momentum, and positions Rotom to wall or burn Metagross. Floette can return later when the Steel threat is handled.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Metagross-Mega (Adamant, Tough Claws) is their primary physical wallbreaker — Ice Punch for Garchomp, Meteor Mash for Fairies, Earthquake for coverage. Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash) enables speed control and Encore disruption. Backline: Stunfisk-Galar (Mimicry terrain tech), Quaquaval (Moxie sweeper), Archaludon (Stalwart anti-redirect), Grimmsnarl (dual screens). Rotom-Wash is a strong Metagross pivot; preserve Floette-Eternal for late-game Fairy Aura sweep. Garchomp must avoid Ice Punch; scout before committing it.

decisions.rationale: Ice Punch + Encore on Talonflame controls the Gale Wings priority threat. If Whimsicott outspeeds, Encore locks Talonflame into failed Tailwind; if Talonflame outspeeds, Brave Bird hits Whimsicott's Focus Sash, then Encore locks it into Brave Bird with recoil. Ice Punch deals 24-77% damage, pressuring Talonflame regardless. Rotom-Wash's Will-O-Wisp is a risk, but controlling Talonflame is priority.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Talonflame (Gale Wings, Sharp Beak) + Rotom-Wash (Levitate, Sitrus Berry). Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird has +1 priority at full HP, OHKO threat to Whimsicott but Focus Sash guarantees survival. Whimsicott's Prankster Encore can lock Talonflame into Tailwind (fails) or Brave Bird (recoil). Metagross-Mega's Ice Punch deals 24-77% to Talonflame. Rotom-Wash's Will-O-Wisp (85% accuracy) is a burn risk to Metagross-Mega. Quaquaval's Moxie snowball is key if given free turns. Archaludon's Stalwart ignores redirection if needed. Opponent's back: Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant), Floette-Eternal (Mega, Flower Veil).

decisions.rationale: Protect blocks IcePunch and Encore aimed at Talonflame, whose Gale Wings is critical. Rotom is nearly unthreatened by Metagross (Levitate blocks EQ, MeteorMash/IcePunch are 0.25x/0.5x) and HydroPump pressures Metagross. Next turn we can BraveBird Whimsicott safely or pivot. Aggressive lines risk Talonflame KO or miss.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Metagross-Mega (Adamant, Tough Claws) physical wallbreaker — IcePunch for Garchomp, MeteorMash for Fairies, EQ for coverage. Whimsicott (Prankster, FocusSash) Encore/Tailwind disruption. Backline: Stunfisk-Galar (Mimicry), Quaquaval (Moxie, LifeOrb), Archaludon (Stalwart, ExpertBelt), Grimmsnarl (Prankster, LightClay screens). Rotom-Wash hard-walls Metagross via Levitate + resistances; preserve Talonflame Gale Wings for late-game. Floette-Eternal is Fairy Aura wincon. Garchomp must avoid IcePunch entirely.

decisions.rationale: Ice Punch into 32% Talonflame is likely KO or forces recoil KO from Encored Brave Bird. Moonblast pressures Rotom-Wash while Whimsicott survives Brave Bird via Focus Sash. Removes Talonflame threat and damages Rotom for optimal board state.
decisions.notebook: Talonflame Gale Wings only active at full HP; Encored into Brave Bird for 3 turns. Whimsicott Focus Sash survives one SE hit. Rotom-Wash Sitrus Berry triggers at 50% HP. Metagross-Mega Ice Punch is SE vs Talonflame (Fire/Flying). Quaquaval Moxie snowball key if given free turns. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection. Opponent back: Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant), Floette-Eternal (Mega, Flower Veil).

decisions.rationale: Talonflame is likely lost to Encore+Ice Punch regardless. BB breaks Whimsicott Sash before Metagross moves. WoW on Metagross is game-changing: burn halves its attack and enables Floette/Garchomp endgame. Even if Talonflame faints, burned Metagross + 1HP Whimsicott leaves me favored with Rotom + backline against crippled threats. Hydro Pump has wider range but burn offers lasting value against their mega.
decisions.notebook: Metagross-Mega (Tough Claws Adamant): primary wallbreaker. Burning it is win-condition-level. Whimsicott: Prankster Encore/Tailwind, Focus Sash must be broken before any sweep. Talonflame: Gale Wings late-game cleaner; preserve only if low-cost. Floette-Eternal: Fairy Aura wincon, needs Metagross neutralized first. Garchomp: 4x Ice-weak; never switch into Metagross. Backline threats unrevealed: Stunfisk-Galar, Quaquaval, Archaludon, Grimmsnarl. Rotom-Wash hard-walls Metagross via Levitate.

Focus fire Garchomp with Ice Punch (4x SE) + Moonblast (2x SE). Combined 98.6-325% damage likely OHKOs even if Garchomp outspeeds. Whimsicott moves first (368 speed), then either Garchomp or Metagross. Whimsicott faints to Earthquake anyway at 1% HP, so maximize damage output. Removing Garchomp eliminates Life Orb Earthquake threat and opens path for Quaquaval/Archaludon cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Talonflame Gale Wings only active at full HP; Encored into Brave Bird for 3 turns. Whimsicott Focus Sash survives one SE hit. Rotom-Wash Sitrus Berry triggers at 50% HP. Metagross-Mega Ice Punch is SE vs Talonflame (Fire/Flying). Quaquaval Moxie snowball key if given free turns. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection. Opponent back: Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant), Floette-Eternal (Mega, Flower Veil). Game 1 strategy: Remove Garchomp early, then use Quaquaval Moxie or Archaludon coverage to clean remaining threats. Rotom-Wash frozen status is temporary advantage.

decisions.rationale: Quaquaval leads to immediately threaten Rotom-Wash with Close Combat for a potential Moxie boost and sweep. Archaludon provides DracoMeteor coverage for Dragapult (breaking Focus Sash with Stalwart) and Thunderbolt for Rotom-Wash. This composition covers all remaining opponent threats and maximizes win conditions through Quaquaval's snowball potential.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Rotom-Wash (56%, no item), Floette-Eternal (Mega, Flower Veil), Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant). Game 1 strategy: Use Quaquaval Moxie to snowball after removing Rotom-Wash, Archaludon breaks Dragapult Sash with DracoMeteor and provides coverage. Talonflame was Encored into Brave Bird and fainted. Garchomp eliminated. Rotom-Wash frozen status was temporary advantage. Quaquaval Moxie key win condition if given free turns. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection for reliable damage.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp guaranteed faster than Metagross; EQ KOs 1% Whimsicott and deals 50-122% to Metagross. Rotom immune via Levitate. Hydro Pump adds 32-87% if thaw (20%). Accept Garchomp may fall to Ice Punch; Floette cleans up damaged Metagross.
decisions.notebook: Metagross-Mega Ice Punch vs Garchomp: 90.7-137.7% (possible OHKO, dangerous range). Burning Metagross is win-condition level. Whimsicott Focus Sash consumed; Prankster Encore threatens Protect-lock. Floette-Eternal: Light of Ruin 140BP Fairy recoil nuke; primary cleaner after Metagross neutralized. Opponent backline unrevealed: Stunfisk-G, Quaquaval, Archaludon, Grimmsnarl.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Aggressive split maximizes KO chances on both threats. Close Combat (61-178%) can OHKO Rotom and trigger Moxie snowball. Flash Cannon (50-131%) can OHKO Floette, removing the biggest threat to Quaquaval. Even if Floette outspeeds and survives Light of Ruin (69.8% min), Quaquaval can still attack. Taking this risk is necessary to activate Moxie win condition.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Quaquaval Moxie is primary win condition, needs KO to snowball. Archaludon Stalwart bypasses redirection for reliable damage. Floette-Eternal Mega is biggest threat with Light of Ruin (140 power, SE to Quaquaval). Rotom-Wash at 56% vulnerable to Close Combat. Opponent remaining: Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant). Strategy: Remove Floette/Rotom quickly, use Quaquaval Moxie boosts to clean up. Archaludon Expert Belt boosts SE hits. Protect Quaquaval when Floette is active and speed uncertain.

decisions.rationale: Protect shields Floette from the most dangerous double-target line (Flash Cannon + Ice Spinner). Mega Evolving now grants Fairy Aura and better stats for the sweep. Will-O-Wisp permanently cripples Quaquaval's Life Orb attacks. Even if they double Rotom, untouched Mega Floette sweeps the remaining foes with Fairy Aura-boosted Light of Ruin.
decisions.notebook: Opponent backline: Grimmsnarl (Light Clay screen setter, Prankster, Careful) and Stunfisk-Galar (Ground/Steel, Leftovers, Impish, Mimicry). Both are defensive; limited offensive pressure once Quaquaval/Archaludon fall. Floette-Mega with Fairy Aura is the win condition — preserve it. Burning Quaquaval neutralizes its Moxie snowball potential. Archaludon Stalwart ignores redirection but that's irrelevant without redirection on my side. Expert Belt on Archaludon makes Flash Cannon a real threat to Floette even through Mega SpD.

decisions.rationale: Quaquaval Protect preserves Moxie win condition against speed uncertainty. Archaludon Flash Cannon is SE with Expert Belt, can OHKO Floette-Mega. If Flash Cannon misses KO, Quaquaval survives to clean up next turn. Aggressive play risks losing primary sweeper to Light of Ruin if outsped.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Quaquaval Moxie primary win condition, needs KO to snowball. Archaludon Stalwart bypasses redirection. Floette-Mega biggest threat with Light of Ruin (140 power, Fairy Aura boost, SE to Quaquaval). Opponent remaining: Floette-Eternal, Dragapult (Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant). Strategy: Remove Floette-Mega with Archaludon Flash Cannon, preserve Quaquaval for cleanup. Protect Quaquaval when speed uncertain or Floette active. Archaludon Expert Belt boosts SE hits. Quaquaval vulnerable at -1 Def/-1 SpD, avoid unnecessary risks.

decisions.rationale: Moonblast guarantees OHKO on 90% Quaquaval (min 92.7% max HP > 90% current HP), 100% acc, no recoil. Floette must remove Quaquaval this turn or perish to +1 LO Liquidation + Expert Belt Flash Cannon. Light of Ruin risks miss and unnecessary recoil. Protect is unreliable after last turn's use. After KO, Flash Cannon does 48-78% leaving Floette alive to win endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent backline: Grimmsnarl (Light Clay, screens, Careful) and Stunfisk-Galar (Leftovers, Impish, Mimicry). Both defensive; limited offensive pressure once Quaquaval/Archaludon fall. Floette-Mega with Fairy Aura is the win condition — preserve it. Quaquaval +1 Atk after Moxie, -1 Def/SpD from Close Combat. Archaludon Expert Belt Flash Cannon is a real threat even through Mega SpD. Remove Quaquaval first to avoid Moxie snowball.

decisions.rationale: Position is lost 1v2 at 13%. Light of Ruin OHKOs Quaquaval but recoil KOs Floette. Moonblast into Quaquaval KOs but Archaludon Flash Cannon KOs Floette. Synthesis to 63% still dies to combined +1 LO Liquidation + Expert Belt Flash Cannon. Only Protect buys a turn without fainting; stall for opponent error (double Protect, Protect failure, or targeting mistake). No winning line exists against optimal play.

Flash Cannon is guaranteed KO on 12% Floette-Mega. Speed order Quaquaval vs Floette-Mega is uncertain (137 vs 117-169). Quaquaval at -1/-1 cannot risk taking Light of Ruin. Protect preserves Moxie win con while Archaludon removes the primary threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Quaquaval Moxie cleanup needs +1 to snowball; preserve at all costs when Floette-Mega active. Archaludon Flash Cannon + Expert Belt reliably KOes Floette-Mega. Floette-Mega Protect success reduced after turn 7 use. Opponent remaining: Floette-Eternal, Dragapult (Focus Sash, Infiltrator), Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant). Post-Floette plan: Quaquaval +1 Atk sweeps with Liquidation/Close Combat; Archaludon provides Stalwart Draco/Flash Cannon support. Quaquaval vulnerable at -1 Def/-1 SpD to priority and fast threats; avoid unnecessary damage. Dragapult Phantom Force 2-turn window exploitable. Annihilape Defiant punishes Intimidate/switch-ins.

decisions.rationale: No line survives a double attack; Moonblast Quaquaval is the only guaranteed value, removing the Moxie threat before fainting. Protect's 33% is worse expected value, and Synthesis still dies to minimum combined damage. Take Quaquaval down and move to game 2.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lost. Notable: Floette-Mega Fairy Aura Moonblast OHKOs Adamant Quaquaval from 90%. Archaludon Expert Belt Flash Cannon does 52-113% to Floette-Mega through 168 SpD. Quaquaval Life Orb Liquidation at +1 does 65-148%. Both backline Grimmsnarl (Light Clay screens, Careful) and Stunfisk-Galar (Leftovers, Impish) are defensive — apply offensive pressure early in game 2. Opponent leads Quaquaval+Archaludon aggressively; consider Talonflame Tailwind + Garchomp Earthquake to outspeed and KO before they set up.

reflections.summary: The game was won because the early trade of Whimsicott and Metagross-Mega for Garchomp removed the opponent's primary physical threat, and Quaquaval's Moxie activation after KO'ing Rotom-Wash provided the +1 Attack needed to pressure Floette-Mega, which was then worn down by Archaludon's super effective Flash Cannon and Protect stalling.
reflections.adjustment: Against Dragapult's Focus Sash and Annihilape's Leftovers recovery, avoid relying on single-hit KOs; use Archaludon's Stalwart Draco Meteor to bypass Protect and apply consistent pressure, while preserving Quaquaval's HP to avoid being picked off by Dragapult's Phantom Force or Annihilape's Close Combat.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leads Garchomp (Life Orb, Rough Skin, Earthquake) + Rotom-Wash (Sitrus Berry, Hydro Pump) or Talonflame + Floette-Mega; Garchomp Earthquakes aggressively; Rotom-Wash spams Hydro Pump; Floette-Mega relies on Protect stalling and Fairy Aura Moonblast. Archaludon Flash Cannon + Expert Belt reliably 2HKOes Floette-Mega; Quaquaval Moxie +1 snowballs after a KO; Floette-Mega Protect success reduces after repeated use (turn 7+). Remaining threats: Dragapult (Focus Sash, Infiltrator, Phantom Force, Will-O-Wisp) and Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant, Rage Fist, Close Combat). Plan: Use Archaludon's Stalwart Draco Meteor to bypass Protect and pressure both; use Quaquaval's Liquidation for high damage on Annihilape; keep Quaquaval healthy due to -1 Def/-1 SpD vulnerability to priority and fast threats.

reflections.summary: We lost because Talonflame fainted early to Whimsicott's Prankster disruption, costing us speed control and leaving a 2v4 deficit. Floette-Mega was then isolated and overwhelmed by Quaquaval's Protect cycles and Archaludon's Stalwart Flash Cannon.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, avoid leading Talonflame into Whimsicott. Instead, lead with a Whimsicott answer (e.g., a Dark-type immune to Prankster or a spread move to break Focus Sash) alongside Garchomp to threaten Metagross and Archaludon. Preserve Floette-Mega to handle Quaquaval after Archaludon is removed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Encore, Tailwind) disrupts speed control. Metagross-Mega (Adamant, Ice Punch) OHKOs Garchomp. Quaquaval (Life Orb Moxie) snowballs; uses Protect frequently. Archaludon (Expert Belt Stalwart) 2HKOs Floette-Mega with Flash Cannon. Backline Grimmsnarl (Light Clay screens) and Stunfisk-Galar (Leftovers) are defensive; not brought G1. Our Talonflame lead was ineffective; do not bring Talonflame if Whimsicott is expected. Future plan: Lead with a Whimsicott answer (Dark-type or multi-hit) + Garchomp to pressure Metagross/Archaludon. Keep Floette-Mega for Quaquaval.
